chunks.heading: Shoot for the Moon
chunks.notes: Opens with a general claim about mothers, then illustrates it with the personal parable of the mother's "shoot for the moon" saying, closing on an aphoristic line.

chunks.heading: Shoot for the Moon
chunks.notes: Confessional fear-of-change material pivots into a generalized claim about modern systems crushing the individual soul, imaged as a field of wildflowers under a tiller.

chunks.heading: Shoot for the Moon
chunks.notes: Argues society's goal (not its brokenness) is the problem, calls the reader to accountability and reclaiming their own narrative.

chunks.heading: Shoot for the Moon
chunks.notes: Two-line closing couplet reframing self-improvement's pain against the strengthening effect of warm gestures given or received.
